assessments.reasoning: GNU’s 1.3 publisher file at [17885,19211) contains §9. Its third paragraph specifies the holder, means, notice history, receipt-based deadline and permanent effect. The surrounding paragraphs distinguish provisional reinstatement on cessation, permanent reinstatement under the separate 60-day condition, and the continued licenses of downstream recipients.

challenge.method: Vary the means of notification, the work and holder in a prior notice, the license concerned, and the cure instant. Compare cure just before and exactly 30 days after receipt with the neighboring cessation provision.
challenge.results: Unreasonable means fail the notice condition. A prior qualifying notice from the same holder about a different work under this License defeats first-notice status. A notice solely from another holder does not exhaust this holder’s first notice. A notice solely about an unrelated license falls outside the stated qualifier. With the other conditions satisfied, cure immediately before 30 days qualifies and cure at exactly 30 days misses this route. The separate 60-day provision measures from cessation.

limitations: The effect of a prior notice under another GNU FDL edition is unresolved here. The clause retains the qualifier “this License.”
An individual case would require evidence of the applicable grant, holder identity, means and receipt of notice, prior notices and time of cure.
reasoning: GNU FDL 1.3 §9 provides permanent reinstatement of the terminated license from the particular notifying holder when that holder gives notice by reasonable means, the licensee has never previously received a qualifying violation notice from that holder for any work under this License, and the licensee cures before 30 days have elapsed from receipt.
